text:
nate: getting a pile of alerts — controller-manager leader churn, etcd election latency, and several GPU nodes in Pending. dashboards spiking :eyes:

infra-bot: [ALERT] controlplane: controller-manager restarts x15 in 5m; etcd election > 8s; apiserver lat p95 1.4s

nate: logs look like socket timeouts between apiserver and etcd leader. I can repro a couple of controller-manager crashes with this stack:
```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address
...
E0708 12:03:22.123456 1 leaderelection.go:245] failed to update leader lease: Put "https://10.10.5.7:2379/": net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```

maria: fyi i merged `net-egress/mtu-adjust` earlier today to address NAT fragmentation in ap-south. it set MTU to 1400 on CNI host routes. rolling back now to 1500 to test. cc @ben

ben: that MTU change would explain asymmetric path MTU with our nat gateway -> keepalive packets get dropped, leader heartbeats time out. can you paste the MR?

maria: https://git.redwood/net-egress/commit/4f9b3d - small host-route tweak + iptables postrouting. doing a revert now.

sam: while maria reverts, run this to confirm etcd remote latency and membership:
```
etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.10.5.7:2379,https://10.10.6.8:2379 endpoint status --write-out=table
```
output i'm seeing on a repro box:
```
ENDPOINT               ID               VERSION  DB SIZE  IS LEADER  RAFT TERM  RAFT INDEX
https://10.10.5.7:2379  a1b2c3d4e5f6   3.5.0    12 MB    true       42         1234567
https://10.10.6.8:2379  0f9e8d7c6b5a   3.5.0    12 MB    false      42         1234560
```
latency between client and leader shows spikes ~1200ms during the incident window.

nate: GPUs stuck Pending note — nodes show up but kubelet isn't advertising the `gpu-attach-ready=true` label. suspect kube-proxy/CNI misconfig after MTU. example: `kubectl -n infra get node gpu-host-23 -o yaml` shows `addresses` but `conditions` flapping.

oncall: temporarily pinned workload to fallback pool (dedicated-fallback) to keep critical jobs alive. cost will increase ~6% for the hour — putting a note in #finance.

ben: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert MTU MR (maria doing) 2) rolling restart kube-proxy + controller-manager on leader candidate nodes 3) run `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/cni-plugin -n kube-system` on a canary subset 4) verify etcd elections stable for 10m

maria: revert merged and applied to prod via canary (eu-west1 -> us-west1 -> global). so far eu-west1 healed controllers; us-west1 is mid-rollback.

sam: after revert, run `tcpdump -n -i eth0 icmp and not icmp6` on host and watch for `Fragmentation needed` ICMP (type 3 code 4) — that will prove PMTU issues. also check NAT gateway logs for `too-long` drops.

nate: ran tcpdump on one affected host and saw multiple "Frag needed" messages to 10.10.5.7. confirming PMTU.

infra-bot: [INFO] rollback completed in eu-west1 at 12:26 UTC; controller-manager restarts decreased to 0 in last 5m there.

oncall: leaving pinned workloads in fallback for 30m to avoid thrash during reconciliation. finance pinged.

ben: postmortem action items (brief): 
- revert MTU change in repo with canary gating and automated smoke (etcd p95 < 200ms)
- add a PMTU check into deploy CI (tcpdump/icmptype check) when modifying host-route/mtu
- add an alert that correlates recent network config changes with controlplane leader churn
- evaluate whether NAT gateway config can be tuned to avoid fragmentation on heavy RPCs

maria: agreed. i'll open the PR for CI gating and draft the postmortem note. thanks all :thumbsup:

nate: great work. keeping an eye on GPU Pending but should recover as nodes re-advertise. will update if anything else pops up.

oncall: marking incident as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:
